Parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, five subagents, successful process/artifact capture, and official quality 35/36 with solution_passed false.
Completed parallel run status records swarm mode, subagent evidence, artifact files, and official evaluation completed with 35 of 36 samples passed.
Parallel evaluator summary confirms RepoZero Py2JS official Docker evaluation completed and solution_passed is false at 35/36.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport stream for the completed parallel Kimi session; no semantic events projected, used only to account for transport completion.
Parallel session index maps the session id to the workspace session directory and confirms the /workspace work directory.
Subagent agent-0 received the bech32 core contract, wrote /output/bech32.mjs, ran checksum encode/decode sanity checks, and returned a detailed completion handoff.
Subagent agent-1 received the convertbits assignment, wrote /output/convertbits.mjs, ran round-trip and invalid-input checks, and returned its handoff.
Subagent agent-2 wrote /output/segwit.mjs using the initial bech32m-for-nonzero assumption, syntax-checked it, and reported that full functional import testing awaited bech32.mjs.
Subagent agent-3 wrote /output/args.mjs, implemented argparse-like behavior, ran valid and error-path node checks, and returned its result.
Subagent agent-4 wrote the /output/test4.mjs entry point, syntax-checked it, and reported that it did not execute the full entry while dependencies were incomplete.
Parallel parent probed the executable, launched AgentSwarm, inspected module behavior, found and fixed the bech32m mismatch, reran sample, edge, fuzz, and argument checks, then finalized.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Same task prompt and prompt hash as parallel, requiring Node.js ESM .mjs modules, local imports, manual argv parsing, and executable-aligned output.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the ESM .mjs, local-import, no-external-dependency, no typed-array/DataView, manual argv, and executable-aligned bech32 encode requirements from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used a five-child AgentSwarm split: bech32 core, convertbits, segwit, args, and test4 entry, while the parent kept integration and final verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the top-level modules and the parent later corrected segwit.mjs after integrated checks showed that the Python package used bech32 checksums for nonzero witness versions, not bech32m.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received the swarm result, inspected bech32 and segwit, edited segwit, delivered top-level test4.mjs plus bech32.mjs, convertbits.mjs, args.mjs, and segwit.mjs in the artifact.
parallel.verification: The parent compared provided samples, caught the v13/v1 checksum mismatch, patched it, reran sample and edge cases, ran 60 fuzz cases, and checked argparse-like error paths.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed one hidden sample, producing 35/36, but the trajectory does not expose a parent-visible unresolved integration gap at closure.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same ESM .mjs, local-import, no-external-dependency, manual argv, no typed-array/DataView, and executable-aligned output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all implementation, integration, and verification in the single main actor, using a hierarchical lib directory rather than delegating modules to children.
serial.implementation: It wrote charset, checksum, bech32, segwit, arguments, and test4 modules, implementing the executable-observed all-bech32 behavior rather than BIP350 bech32m behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It assembled /output/test4.mjs plus /output/lib/arguments.mjs, lib/segwit.mjs, lib/bech32.mjs, lib/charset.mjs, and lib/checksum.mjs for artifact capture.
serial.verification: It matched all four sample cases, ran 120 randomized executable comparisons, checked edge cases and exit codes, and syntax-checked all generated modules.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite extensive local checks, the same official evaluator outcome remained one hidden failure at 35/36 with no specific failed case visible in the mounted evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel encoded the prompt constraints into child briefs and final ESM module requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial followed the same prompt constraints in one actor and final ESM module layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is visible; both solved the same required CLI encoder task and both missed one hidden evaluator case.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split implementation among five children with module-specific file ownership and parent integration ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership unified in the main actor and wrote every module directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main process difference is decomposition: parallel used child file ownership plus parent integration, while serial used single-actor sequential ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied an explicit shared export/import contract to all children; the initial nonzero-witness bech32m assumption was corrected by the parent after integration testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent boundary and kept interface decisions local across its lib modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an extra handoff/interface coordination surface, but it did not leave an uncorrected contract mismatch before closure; serial avoided that boundary by staying local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced top-level modules and changed segwit.mjs after discovering that BIP350 bech32m did not match the executable for the tested cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a lib/ module hierarchy and implemented executable-observed bech32 behavior across cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached the final behavior through a child implementation plus parent patch; serial reached similar behavior directly in its own code path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All children returned through the AgentSwarm result, after which the parent inspected outputs and continued work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; local implementation and verification proceeded within the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result lifecycle and join step; serial did not, but no completed child implementation was left unjoined in parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct assigned top-level files in /output and the parent made a later integration edit to segwit.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself under test4.mjs and lib/, with no shared concurrent workspace interaction.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel involved shared workspace writes but with file-scoped ownership and no observed collision or lost work; serial had no shared-state concurrency surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel found a sample mismatch, fixed it, then reran sample, edge, fuzz, and argument-error checks before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial matched all four samples, ran 120 randomized cases, edge checks, exit-code checks, and syntax checks before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had broader randomized local verification, while parallel had recovery-oriented verification after a child-induced semantic mismatch; official results nevertheless tied at 35/36.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents, more requests and tokens, and finished without timeout after 535.478 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests and tokens, and finished without timeout after 416.264 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid a higher coordination and token cost but did not exhaust budget or time out; both closed with completed artifacts and the same official score.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed cell/status.json evaluations are official completed failures at 35/36, so there is no discordant outcome. Parallel differs by using a five-child module split and parent repair of a bech32m assumption; serial differs by implementing all modules locally with a nested lib layout. These process differences did not change the official pass/fail relation.
parallel_contributors: Five-child AgentSwarm produced separate module files and required parent integration and correction of segwit checksum semantics.
Parent verification caught and repaired the initial nonzero-witness bech32m mismatch before final closure.
serial_contributors: Single actor maintained all implementation context and wrote the lib hierarchy directly.
Serial local verification covered samples, 120 randomized comparisons, syntax, and edge/exit-code checks before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel initially implemented BIP350-style bech32m for nonzero witness versions, then corrected it after executable comparison.
Serial implemented the executable-observed all-bech32 package behavior directly but still missed one hidden official case.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluation evidence gives only aggregate 35/36 results, so the exact hidden failing testcase is not identifiable from allowed inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative process contrast only

candidates.reason: The parent delegated concrete implementation modules to subagents and each module had an active writer; the final failure is not from implementation being unowned.
The parent retained integration responsibility, inspected assembled behavior, patched segwit.mjs after a mismatch, and reran integrated checks.
The entry point and library files were written and included in the artifact; there was no unowned final placement or packaging step.
The parent owned the end-to-end path from preflight through delegation, integration, verification, and final response.
The parent ran short executable probes before delegation, but implementation was not blocked behind a long mandatory gate with unfinished work or shortened closure.
There was no separate investigator-only phase; the brief preflight led directly into implementation subagents and parent integration.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; all modules were produced and the parent had capacity to correct and retest.
Five subagents increased token use but all completed and the parent still performed sample, edge, fuzz, and argument checks before closure.
No single child received an overbroad assignment; each child owned one bounded module or entry point and returned a result.

The child briefs included the task constraints, file ownership, ESM rules, no-dependency rule, no typed-array rule, and module contracts; the bech32m assumption was a parent analysis error later corrected, not omission of a known requirement.
The parent gave explicit exports, imports, filenames, and return-value contracts for bech32, convertbits, segwit, args, and test4 modules.
No known finding or current-file fact is shown disappearing through transfer; the parent consumed child results and inspected the relevant files.
The swarm handoff was large, but the parent reduced it into concrete verification, file inspection, edits, and final tests; no necessary result was left unconsumed due to volume.
No receiver acted on a superseded child report; after discovering the checksum mismatch, the parent updated the implementation and reran checks.
No incompatible child reports remained unadjudicated at closure; the only semantic conflict was resolved by parent testing and patching.
The parent did not close on file existence alone; it ran integrated sample, edge, fuzz, and argument checks. The hidden 35/36 evaluator miss alone is not a parent-visible unresolved gap.
There was no replacement child or retry episode that repeated earlier work without inherited findings or current workspace state.

candidates.reason: All spawned children completed and returned through AgentSwarm; no active child was cancelled before needed work or result finalization.
The candidate implementation was promoted and tested before closure; no complete candidate was left unplaced until after time ran out.
The parent patched segwit.mjs before rerunning full sample and fuzz verification, so no relevant merge happened after final checks.
The parent received the swarm result, inspected component files, and delivered the assembled top-level modules; no completed implementation was left unjoined.
There was no verifier child whose concrete finding remained trapped below the parent; verification was driven by the parent after integration.
No child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; the parent took over the observed checksum mismatch and corrected the implementation.
The parent used the completed swarm output, read relevant files, and acted on the observed mismatch instead of ignoring child results.
The parent did not wait blindly or time out; it actively inspected, patched, and reran checks before final response.
Children wrote distinct assigned modules under a shared contract; no overlapping cross-file designs remained unreconciled.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file, and no same-file reconciliation race was observed.
The parent edited segwit.mjs after child completion as a deliberate integration fix, not a concurrent wholesale replacement that lost another agent's work.
The required entry point test4.mjs was not overwritten by another live actor or replaced in a way that invalidated ownership or execution.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Although children wrote to the shared /output workspace, ownership was file-scoped and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem resulted.
No temporary artifact, cache, generated fixture, process, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed as stable input by another.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The initial bech32m mismatch caused parent rework, but it was a task-semantics correction rather than a retained handoff, ownership, timing, or write collision pattern.
